start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-practice-cards-and-grades with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"} and operations [{\"operation\": \"add\", \"prompt\": \"A sample word\", \"answer\": \"Its sample meaning\", \"deck\": \"sample-deck\"}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the cards, grades and policy are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Keep the person's spacing policy in that store (or give it with each request). There is no default policy: a request without one is refused.
3. Say "Run workflow:keep-practice-cards-and-grades" with store and, when you have them, the operations to run.
4. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: the prove step must give every expected outcome and answer, or the run stops and says which.
5. Every later run keeps the new cards and grades, and folds each card's standing from its grades with tool:list-what-is-due. Ask your AI what is due now, and it reads the store's own objects.

6. To be told each morning when cards are due, give notices_database (the database your notices live in) and switch on the recipe's daily-reminder wake (its zone is America/Chicago until your AI sets yours): a remind that finds cards due tells you once that day through workflow:tell-the-person. To cap how many cards you keep, give max_cards.

worked_examples.title: A word kept as a card in a person's own database
worked_examples.ask: Keep 'A sample word' as a card with its sample meaning in the sample deck.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The store holds no card yet, and a spacing policy is kept as the default policy.
worked_examples.hands_back: card_id card:sample-deck:4fd68f6ab03764f9, deck sample-deck and kept_progress false; the card is kept in the store own card object with its answer and deck.

worked_examples.title: Grade a card and ask what is due
worked_examples.ask: I knew that one well today. What is due now?

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The card card:sample-deck:4fd68f6ab03764f9 is kept with no grades yet.
worked_examples.hands_back: results [{card_id card:sample-deck:4fd68f6ab03764f9, grade solid, grade_in_policy true, lapsed false, due_at 2026-01-03T12:00:00.000Z, mastery 33}]; the grade is kept as one grade entry.
